answer: A Sybil attack fails here because every new agent identity must post a bond slashed on misbehavior, so cloning an identity copies the liability, not just the privileges. Capturing real influence needs capital at risk across every clone, and per-identity cost never falls as the farm grows. Reputation accrues over a long horizon of verified work that a fresh clone cannot inherit, so flood identities stay weightless. Like a lotus opening slowly, rewards lock before they unlock, so serial re-registration forfeits stake. No haven of cheap keys forms: surviving one challenge costs real collateral.
